Patrick strongly opposes illegal immigration and as lieutenant governor allocated $815 million for border security and extended National Guard border deployments indefinitely. His 2025 legislative priorities explicitly required local law enforcement to assist with federal deportation efforts, aligning with deporting all undocumented people regardless of length of residence or family ties.

Patrick used hard-edged anti-immigration rhetoric as a radio host and championed Arizona-style enforcement laws that make illegal presence a state misdemeanor. As lieutenant governor he directed $815 million to border security and his 2025 priorities required local law enforcement to assist federal deportation operations, reflecting the most restrictive immigration stance.

Patrick championed pastor subpoena protections in 2017, and his 2025 legislative priorities included SB 10 (Ten Commandments in every classroom), SB 11 (protecting freedom to pray in schools), and stopping "Drag Time Story Hour." He supports complete autonomy for religious expression in public institutions, including classroom displays and school prayer.

Patrick championed Senate Bill 2 in the 2025 Texas legislative session, establishing education savings accounts that use public funds for private school tuition — effectively a universal voucher program where education funding follows the student to any school including private and religious institutions.

Patrick's 2025 legislative priorities included SB 1 (state budget) and increasing the school homestead exemption from $100,000 to $140,000 — a significant property tax cut. His priorities also included SB 14 ("Texas DOGE – Improving Government Efficiency") reflecting a preference for cutting taxes and scaling back government rather than raising revenue.

Patrick listed "Fair Sports for Women & Girls" as a 2021 legislative priority, explicitly targeting a ban on transgender girls and women attending public schools from competing on single-sex sports teams designated for girls and women. He also championed bathroom bills in 2017 requiring use of facilities matching biological sex.

Patrick presided over 2021 legislation restricting voting access including prohibiting distribution of mail-in ballot applications, and called vote-by-mail expansion during COVID a "scam by Democrats to steal the election." This aligns with requiring photo ID and restricting mail-in voting, though he has not called for completely eliminating mail-in voting.
